coverage.main: Read all ten pages of arXiv 2011.09957v1 (19 November 2020; CVPR Workshops 2021): Sections 1-5, Tables 1-5, Figures 1-7 and references. The CVPRW version of record was not retrieved.
coverage.supplement: No appendix; only a video-example website is linked.
coverage.excluded_results: Diagonal (victim = test model) cells of Tables 3-5 are white-box. Table 1 reports detector AUC on the DFDC test set (setup). Figures 1-5 and 7 are qualitative.

result_groups.locator: Section 4.1 Evaluation Metrics; Tables 3-4 off-diagonal cells
result_groups.population: First 100 fake and 100 real DFDC validation videos (30,300 frames); per-frame attacks (plain iterative and transformation-based transfer attack) crafted on one of four detectors and evaluated on the others
result_groups.outcome: success rate: 'the percentage of videos for which we are able to successfully flip the original correct label predicted by a given detection method'; 'we do not take into account the videos that are originally mis-predicted by the classifier'
result_groups.evidence: Videos each test detector originally mispredicts are explicitly excluded. No victim-success rule is stated; the victim diagonals are 100% except 99.0% in Table 4.

result_groups.locator: Section 3.5; Section 4 universal paragraph; Table 5 off-diagonal; Figure 6
result_groups.population: Universal perturbations trained on 100 separate DFDC training videos at epsilon = 40/255 (and a sweep in Figure 6), evaluated on the same evaluation videos and unseen detectors
result_groups.evidence: The same success-rate definition excludes originally mispredicted videos; a universal perturbation has no per-video victim-success filter stated.

f1.evidence: Detection AUC on the DFDC test set is reported for each detector, but no clean accuracy on the 200 evaluation videos is printed (only used to exclude mispredicted videos).

f2.evidence: Originally mispredicted videos are excluded for each detection method. Positive conditioning evidence.

f4.evidence: Denominators vary with each detector's correctly predicted videos and are not stated (e.g., 68.75%).

f5.evidence: L-infinity epsilon = 16/255 for per-frame attacks (transfer attack uses the same hyperparameters) and 40/255 with a sweep for universal perturbations; measured mean L-infinity is also reported.

f6.evidence: Only a video-example site is linked; detectors are public DFDC entries, but the attack code is not identified.

artifact_checks.result: Downloaded and hashed; the paper links deepfakeattacks.github.io (examples) and third-party detector repositories only. The example site was not accessed.

bounds_checks.reason: Rates exclude originally mispredicted videos, so they are conditional on clean correctness.
